# dm/third_party: third-party code

This is code written by others, shipped with the repository so there is nothing to download. Each component keeps its original license, and the license file sits in its own directory.

| Directory | What it is | Version and changes | Where it is used | License file |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `flip/` | NVIDIA FLIP, an image difference metric that models human viewing. `FLIP.h` plus the source of the command-line tool in `tool/` | Not recorded in the directory | Verification: the image quality measurements in `dm/verify/gfxq/`; build `flip` first with `make -C dm/third_party/flip` | `flip/LICENSE` (BSD 3-Clause) |
| `dav1d/` | The AV1 decoder dav1d: the C sources, headers and arm64 NEON assembly an arm64 build compiles, with the configuration meson generates in `config/` and per-bit-depth wrappers of its templates in `config/tmpl/` | 1.5.4 (upstream commit `54706fc`), unmodified | Host: decodes the games' AV1 movies where VideoToolbox has no AV1 decoder (`dm/host/hle_movie_av1.c`). `dm/host/Makefile` builds it into `gen/dav1d/libdav1d.a`; the iOS build compiles the same files | `dav1d/COPYING` (BSD 2-Clause) |
| `libvpx/` | The VP9 decoder from libvpx: the 71 source files a VP9-decoder-only build compiles, their headers, and the generated configuration in `config/` | v1.17.0 (upstream commit `6df3ec3`), unmodified | Host: decodes the games' VP9 movies (`dm/host/hle_movie.c`). `dm/host/Makefile` builds it into `gen/vpx/libvpx.a`; the iOS build compiles the same files | `libvpx/LICENSE` (BSD 3-Clause), with the patent grant in `libvpx/PATENTS` |
| `stb_vorbis/` | Ogg Vorbis decoder, a single file `stb_vorbis.c` | 1.22 (upstream commit `1ee679c`), unmodified | Host: decodes the Vorbis sound tracks of the games' WebM movies (`dm/host/hle_movie.c`, which includes the file with its push-data API only) | `stb_vorbis/LICENSE` (MIT or public domain, your choice; the same text ends `stb_vorbis.c`) |
| `ryujinx/` | The shader translation library from Ryujinx, three projects: `Ryujinx.Graphics.Shader`, `Ryujinx.Common`, `Spv.Generator` | Ryujinx 1.3.2, with the local changes listed in `ryujinx/README.md` | Referenced by the shader translation tool `dm/gfx/tools/dmsh_xlate`, which translates the original Switch shaders to SPIR-V | `ryujinx/LICENSE.txt` (MIT); `ryujinx/src/Spv.Generator/LICENSE` is that subproject's own license text |

A few more notes:

- `flip/tool/` also carries three single-header libraries used by the FLIP command-line tool: `stb_image.h` (2.23), `stb_image_write.h` (1.13) and `tinyexr.h`. Their license notices are in the files themselves.
- `dav1d/README.md`, `libvpx/README.md`, `stb_vorbis/README.md` and `ryujinx/README.md` record where each came from and what it is used for.
- Six pieces of third-party code live outside this directory:
  - The code nxnative started from. nxnative began as a copy of the generic parts of [d2r-mobile](https://github.com/jhaizhou-ops/d2r-mobile) by jhaizhou (MIT), in nxnative's first commit `d1b17080`: the NSO rewriter, the host that stands in for Horizon, the NVN-on-Metal layer and the iOS app shell. Much of it has been rewritten since, but some is still as it came (about 900 lines of `dm/gfx/nvn/hle_nvn.c`, for example). Its license text is `d2r-mobile/LICENSE`.
  - `dm/gfx/nvn/include/nvn.h` (MIT, by h1k421, named in the file header).
  - The layout size algorithm in `dm/gfx/nvn/nvn_tex.c`, ported from deko3d by fincs (zlib license, notice at the head of the file).
  - Two adapted from MacNativeGames (MIT, license text in `macnativegames/LICENSE`): in `dm/gfx/nvn/nvn_mtl.m` the GPU widening of 8-bit indices (`wide_*`) and the in-pass clear triangles (`clear_color_tri` / `clear_ds_tri`), from its `widen_u8_gpu` and `clear_quad` / `clear_ds_quad`, and the Tears of the Kingdom visibility-counter lowering in `dm/gfx/tools/dmsh_xlate/Program.cs` (`VertexCounterLowering`).
  - The integer timer and camera helpers of Astral Chain's frame step in `dm/games/01007300020FA000/patches.py`, adapted from [AstralChain-Dynamic-FPS](https://github.com/yogesh1239/AstralChain-Dynamic-FPS) v1.1.1 by yogesh1239 (MIT). The license text is at the head of the file.
- Three native executables are committed, so building an IPA needs no compiler for them. Each has its license texts beside it:
  - `dm/gfx/tools/spirv_cross_bin/spirv-cross`: SPIRV-Cross by the Khronos Group, built by `build.sh` in the same folder. Apache-2.0 (some headers MIT or Khronos), with its `LICENSE` and `LICENSES/` copied beside it.
  - `dm/gfx/tools/dmsh_xlate_bin/dmsh_xlate`: the shader translator. Ryujinx's shader library (`ryujinx/`), MacNativeGames' visibility-counter lowering and the .NET runtime (MIT, by the .NET Foundation and Contributors) are compiled into it. See `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt` beside it.
  - `dm/tools/nx_extract_bin/nx_extract`: the NSP extractor. [LibHac 0.19.0](https://www.nuget.org/packages/LibHac/0.19.0) by Alex Barney (MIT) and the .NET runtime are compiled into it. See `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt` beside it.
  - The .NET runtime in both C# tools brings code of its own, such as zlib-ng. Its notices are in [the runtime's THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.TXT](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.TXT).
- The button glyphs of the iOS app's controller hints are not code: five SVGs from "Switch Button Icons and Controls" by Zacksly (CC BY 3.0, <https://zacksly.itch.io>), unmodified, drawn recoloured in NX 18's colours. They are in `dm/ios/Resources/ButtonIcons` with the licence (`LICENSE.txt`) and a README that says which pack files they are and how the app uses them; the credit is shown in the app (under the settings and in About this game) and in the top-level README.
- Two of the host's own Metal shaders (`dm/gfx/msl`, compiled into the app by `dm/gfx/tools/host_msl.py`) are ported from others' shaders, each with its notice at the head of the port:
  - `cmaa2.metal`, the present's edge smoothing (`DM_POST_AA`): a hand port of Intel's Conservative Morphological Anti-Aliasing 2.3, `CMAA2.hlsl` from [GameTechDev/CMAA2](https://github.com/GameTechDev/CMAA2) (Apache-2.0; the full license text is `cmaa2/LICENSE`; the changes are listed at the top of the file, as the license asks). Its R11G11B10 packing comes from Microsoft's MiniEngine (`PixelPacking_R11G11B10.hlsli`, MIT), as in CMAA2.hlsl, with that attribution kept.
  - `fs_rcas` in `present.metal`, the present's Sharpening (`DM_PRESENT_SHARPEN`): ported from `ffx_fsr1.h` of AMD's FidelityFX FSR 1.0 (MIT, the notice in the file).
